topic: Adaptive Orchestration: Runtime Topology Switching Based on Task-Structure Estimation
hypothesis: AdaptOrch improves task success rate by 10-20% over static best-topology assignment by switching orchestration topologies at runtime based on execution trace features. Real tasks shift D-I-T (decomposability, iterativeness, tool-diversity) characteristics mid-execution, and a system that detects these phase transitions and switches to the topology best suited for the current phase outperforms any single static topology.

success_criteria.experiment: Implement a runtime topology switching system with 3+ canonical topologies (hierarchical, flat conversation, debate), a D-I-T feature extractor operating on execution traces, a contextual bandit switching policy, and a shared state transfer protocol. Evaluate on SWE-bench, GAIA, and WebArena tasks that exhibit within-task structural shifts.
success_criteria.expected_improvement: 10-20% task success rate improvement over static best-topology baseline. Demonstrate that switching decisions correlate with ground-truth phase boundaries and that switching overhead is below 5% of total execution time.
success_criteria.metrics: Task success rate, switching precision/recall at phase boundaries, switching overhead (latency), token efficiency, per-phase topology-task alignment score. Statistical significance via paired bootstrap (p<0.05).

concurrent_work.paper: AdaptOrch: Task-Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration in the Era of LLM Performance Convergence (Yu, 2026, arXiv 2602.16873)
concurrent_work.relationship: Validates our premise (topology > model choice) but uses static per-task assignment. Our work addresses runtime switching, which their approach cannot handle.
concurrent_work.differentiation: We switch topologies mid-execution based on execution trace features. They select topology once per task based on task metadata. Our approach handles within-task structural shifts that static assignment misses.
